heads.text: MILITIA OF ONE MEETS ARMY OF MANY
TOTAL WAR, NOW WITH TOTAL GOBLINS
NINE EMPTY SLOTS VS. ONE HORDE

caps.text: {enemy} on the march, drawn by a refugee who would very much like his house back.
The {enemy} vanguard. The front one is labelled 'total'; the rest are labelled 'war'.
Our militia at full strength: one captain, nine dotted outlines and a bed.
The gate, defended by a thousand armor stands. None have armor. None have legs that move.
Goblin banner reading, roughly, 'SEARABBEYS WAS NICE. YOURS NEXT.'
The horde as seen from the Safety burrow, which the artist insists is safe this time.
A goblin standard-bearer, smiling in a way the artist found upsetting.
Trolls passing the windmills. One stopped to admire the mist ring. We wish it hadn't.
The captain, mid-yawn, on hearing the word 'siege'. Status at time of sketch: Off duty.
The mayor serving a production order violation on the goblins. They did not sign it.
Goblin engineers measuring our walls. Unlike us, they finished the smoothing.
Artist's map of the approach. Every route ends at the throne room, where a hundred thrones wait.

reps.text: Lookouts identify the banners of {enemy}, last seen emptying three towns in a single season. Refugees among us have begun packing out of habit.
{civ} remains at war with {enemy}, which the attackers appear to have read about and taken personally.
The militia captain was informed of the siege and remained Off duty, as per the schedule. The nine empty places in the squad have also failed to report.
The Overseer has answered the siege by queuing eleven hundred armor stands. Asked how they would help, the management said armor stands have an intimidating silhouette.
Elders recall {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. 'We lost the fort, the drinks and the artifact,' said one. 'Mostly I miss the drinks.'
Citizens are directed to the Safety burrow. Citizens who remember the last Safety burrow are directed wherever they personally feel safest, such as the tavern.
{who} spotted the horde first and told the captain, who was asleep, then the mayor, who filed a form, then the bookkeeper, who counted the goblins twice.
Goblin numbers are estimated at 'enough'. Our stockpile holds 2,000 drinks, which experts say is plenty to die of thirst beside, comfortably.
The outpost liaison writes that there is much to share and recommends an import agreement for spears. Delivery is expected next autumn, or after the siege, whichever is later.
Haulers were ordered to stop gathering plants on the far side of the map. They are currently on the far side of the map, near the goblins, gathering plants.
{civ} is at peace with most of the world. Regrettably, 'most' does not include the ones standing outside our gate holding torches.
Skirmishers of The High Cruelties were seen arguing with a Destined Wickedness squad over who got to besiege {fort} first. Both lost the argument to a muddy slope.
The goblins arrived during {season}, a season known for its weather. Defensive preparations include smoothing the floor the goblins will be standing on.
The execution tower has been declared open. The hammerer's office remains vacant, so any goblin wishing to be punished must fill in the form personally.

kickers.text: The militia will be informed when it wakes up.
Refugees from the burned towns: please do not unpack yet.
A throne has been queued for the goblin general, as a courtesy.
Remember {past_fort}. Then remember where you left the axes.
The Safety burrow is open. The Herald is staying upstairs.
Import agreement for courage pending. Much to share, apparently.
Goblins are reminded that smoothed floors are slippery.
The mayor's paperwork will be served on the horde at dawn.

heads.text: BEAST WALKS PAST CAPTAIN, OFF DUTY
MIST RING FAILS TO CHEER MONSTER

caps.text: The beast, mid-staircase, thirty levels down. The artist's legs were moving the whole time.
A forgotten beast. The bookkeeper is already trying to forget it, on purpose.
A crooked horror, after descriptions of Omo Fewethauyira. More crooked in person.
The Safety burrow sign, now facing the wrong way. Most residents agree it always was.
The creature passing a row of armor stands, which it mistook for an audience.
The beast inspecting the cistern. We will be boiling the water for a while.
Footprints in the freshly smoothed corridor. The smoother has been told and is weeping.
The monster's breath, shown as a cloud. Its smell, at the editor's request, is not shown.
Our militia confronting the beast. The space where the militia would be is in pencil.
The beast pausing at the garbage pit, which even it declined to enter.
Thone Nìnoana, from a traveller's description. The traveller declined to elaborate.
The creature, sketched from the top of a tree. The artist has since been told about trees.

reps.text: A forgotten beast has left the caverns and, consulting no map, found the deepest burrow full of dwarves at once. Residents: the Safety burrow is a name, not a promise.
Survivors of an earlier fort recall fifteen dwarves sheltering in a burrow named Safety, thirty levels down, when something walked up the stairs. 'Location,' they say.
The beast was last seen near the windmills. The Overseer has kept the haulers gathering plants nearby, on the theory that the beast cannot see dwarves who are busy.
Travellers report the crooked horror Omo Fewethauyira still lurks near Shadyghosts. This beast is not that one, which the Herald finds only slightly comforting.
{who} met the creature first and called it 'a lot of beast for one corridor.' The patient is recovering in one of our hospitals, the one with a doctor.
The militia captain has been alerted and remains Off duty. A runner was sent to wake him. The runner has also taken a nap, citing solidarity.
Engineers propose sealing the stairs. The Overseer counter-proposes smoothing them so the beast may slip. Both jobs are queued behind the other ten thousand.
The hide is described as 'like the inside of a cave, but walking.' The leatherworker asked if it would tan nicely and has been asked to leave the meeting.
Experts advise hiding in a sealed room with food and drink. Experts further advise actually drinking the drink, a step that has historically been skipped.
So far the creature has destroyed two doors, one well and a lifetime of stockpile organisation. The armor stands, as ever, are untouched.
Scholars of {fort} say it is the first of its kind seen here. Scholars in the tavern say it is the first of its kind seen anywhere, and that they need another drink.
The mist ring has been left running in hopes of calming the beast with happy thoughts. Early reports suggest the beast is now damp, and still a beast.
Elves have sent condolences from their forest retreat, observing that the beast is 'a living part of nature'. The beast has since eaten the letter.
A thing has risen from the dark below {fort}. The Overseer has added 'deal with thing' to the work orders, just below the latest throne.

kickers.text: Do not go down to Safety. We cannot stress this enough.
The beast's name will be learned the hard way.
Hospital two of four has a doctor; please get hurt there.
Please do not climb a tree to escape. We have been over this.
The captain will be told after the nap.
Stairs are now considered a two-way street.
Seal the caverns, the Herald begs, gently.
Elves say it is nature. Elves say a lot.

heads.text: DWARF DIES OF THIRST, BESIDE ALE
FORT LOSES ONE MORE TO DUTY

caps.text: The deceased's last view: two thousand drinks, unlabelled and therefore untouched.
Memorial sketch. The rough gems in the background are not symbolic. They were there.
The tree in question. It has been asked to explain itself, and has not.
The Safety burrow entrance, now marked with a second, smaller sign: 'Not.'
The garbage pit, viewed from a respectful distance and a strong wind.
The deceased's mug, which was full the whole time, in the next room.
The hospital where the dwarf was taken. This is one of the ones without a doctor.
The coffin, from a runaway coffin order that turned out, for once, to be the useful one.
Mourners at the slab. One is nervously checking the drinks stockpile, for herself.
Artist's tribute. The thirst-themed border was the editor's idea; the family did not object.
The deceased's workshop, as left, with a half-made armor stand nobody will finish.
The tomb, smoothed to a high shine by a smoother with nothing better queued. He did.

reps.text: {first} died of thirst this week. At the time the fortress held over two thousand drinks, most a short walk away and none of them, apparently, the right one.
The Herald recalls Bomrek Enshalcatten of Searabbeys, found dead, dehydrated, beside 1,994 drinks. Scholars call it the thirst paradox. The dead have other words for it.
{first} was hauling refuse back out of the garbage pit when more refuse came down. The Overseer has called the incident 'circular' and queued another haul.
Friends say {first} climbed a tree to fetch a log and simply never came down. Miners are again reminded that trees go up, and dwarves belong down.
The cause of death is listed as 'Safety'. Officials clarify this means the burrow, not the general concept, though the general concept is also under review.
{first} was carried to a hospital with beds, splints and a traction bench, but no doctor, as the chief medical dwarf's office remains vacant.
Colleagues remember {first} as tireless. The job log agrees: seventy smoothing jobs in a row, no breaks, no meals, no drink, every one perfectly smooth.
Veterans of {past_fort} swear a carpenter there died of thirst beside a heap of rough gems. 'He couldn't drink them,' said one. 'But you could see him thinking about it.'
The mayor has posthumously cited {first} for a production order violation. The fine is procedural and will come out of the coffin budget.
The population of {fort} is now {pop}. The bookkeeper has recounted three times, sighed twice, and checked the drinks once, just in case.
A slab will be engraved once the mason finishes an armor stand order the Overseer considers 'very important'. Estimated completion: stand two thousand.
Witnesses agree the deceased walked past the well, the tavern and a barrel to reach the far side of the map and pick one strawberry, in the rain.
In lieu of flowers, the family asks that citizens go and have a drink right now, on purpose, while they still can.
The death has been ruled 'fortress-related'. The Herald offers condolences and a reminder that the cistern is full and nobody will be cross if you use it.

kickers.text: Please drink something today. Anything. The Herald insists.
{first} is survived by 2,000 drinks, all unopened.
The tree has been questioned and released.
Trees: not even once.
Safety burrow tours are suspended indefinitely.
Do not haul anything out of the garbage pit. Ever.
The Overseer sends condolences, and a work order.
A doctor is wanted; inquire at any of our four hospitals.

heads.text: CAT ADOPTS DWARF, FILES NO FORM
BEST FRIEND FOUND, NOT IN A TREE
DWARF FINDS LOVE, IT HAS FUR

caps.text: The new pet, asleep on a throne. There are hundreds of them, so nobody minded.
Owner and pet in the tavern. Only one of them was told the drinks were free.
The pet guarding a rough gem. Moody dwarves are advised to ask nicely.
The animal visiting the barracks, raising militia attendance by one hundred per cent.
Owner and pet beside the mist ring. Both are damp. Both claim happiness.
The pet refusing to enter the Safety burrow. Experts call it our smartest citizen.
The animal's chosen bed: inside an armor stand. Finally, a use.
The pet sniffing the garbage pit. It came back out, which is more than some managed.
The pet greeting a merchant, who has been asked to stop haggling over it.
Portrait of the happy pair, with the pet drawn larger at the pet's insistence.
Owner, pet, and the mayor's citation for unlicensed adoption, in that order.
The pet watching the moat. The moat watching back has not been confirmed.

reps.text: {who} has adopted an animal companion. Elders of {past_fort} still speak of its dogs with the pride usually reserved for drinks.
The new pet drinks from the well every day, making it, by the bookkeeper's reckoning, the best-hydrated resident of {fort}.
The militia captain has offered the pet a place in the squad, as there are nine vacancies. The pet accepted and immediately went Off duty.
The mayor's office has charged the pet with a production order violation for producing nothing. The pet has responded by sleeping on the charge sheet.
Vets, of whom we have none, say the pet should be kept away from trees, deep burrows and the garbage pit, which is also the Herald's advice to dwarves.
The pet has been offered the vacant office of sheriff. Officials note it is the first candidate in years to show interest, though the interest was mostly in the chair.
{who} says the animal is loyal, brave and a good listener. Asked to name one other resident of {fort} with all three, the owner went quiet.
The Overseer has marked the adoption by queuing eleven pet beds and fifteen hundred food bowls. The order is believed to be running away already.
Passing elves praised the adoption as 'a bond with nature.' Our dwarves praised it as 'a thing that might bite goblins.' Both parties left happy.
The pet has toured the hospitals, sniffing three without doctors and one with. It preferred the doctor, and growled at the vacant office.
The pair were seen sharing a meal in the dining hall. Of the {pop} residents, the pet is reportedly the only one with no complaints.
Old soldiers recall a dog at {past_fort} that knew the way to every throne by smell. 'Hundreds of them,' they say. 'Every one, sniffed.'
Neighbours report the pet barks at the cistern, the windmills and the Overseer's notice board, which several dwarves call the bravest thing anyone has done.
The pet's first official act was to steal a sausage from the butcher, ending what some had begun calling the great meat shortage.

kickers.text: The pet could not be reached; it was asleep on a throne.
{first} requests the pet be addressed as 'sir'.
The pet is not available for the sheriff's job. Yet.
Keep pets out of trees, burrows and pits, as with dwarves.
Searabbeys had thirteen dogs. We have ambitions.
The pet is drinking enough. Learn from the pet.
Petting is permitted. Adoption forms are, regrettably, mandatory.
Militia strength now two, counting paws.

heads.text: DWARF SNAPS AFTER ROUGH GEM HUNT
MILITIA OF ONE ASKED TO HELP
RAMPAGE IN THE MIST RING ZONE

caps.text: The berserker, mid-swing, beside a sign reading 'DAYS SINCE LAST INCIDENT: 0'.
A dented throne, one of hundreds. Nobody has yet worked out which one.
The cause, per witnesses: a production order violation slip, now in pieces.
The berserker in the plant-gathering fields, in the rain, which did not help.
The militia's response, drawn as a closed bedroom door marked 'Off duty'.
Witnesses hiding behind the armor stands, the first defence they have ever offered.
The tavern after the rampage. The ale survived. The ale always survives.
A smoothed wall, now rough again. The smoother has been told and has also snapped.
The berserker, glimpsed near the execution tower. The hammerer's chair: empty.
Victims recovering in a hospital with no doctor, attended by a sympathetic cat.
The mist ring, spraying happy thoughts at the berserker. Result: a wet berserker.
Artist's diagram of the tantrum spiral. It is a spiral. It is going down.

reps.text: {who} has gone berserk after what friends call 'the four hundredth smoothing job, the third missed meal and a dream about a drink.' Bystanders are asked to stand further by.
It began when the moody dwarf next door was handed the last rough gem. {first} had wanted it for nothing in particular, and that, friends say, was the point.
The militia captain has been asked to subdue the berserker. The militia captain is Off duty. The nine other squad positions remain a matter of philosophy.
The rage began in the dining hall over the last roast and ended in the throne room, where at least eleven of the hundred-odd thrones were knocked over.
Officials note {first} was not thirsty, not hungry and not in a burrow called Safety. It was, the doctors would say if we had any, just a very bad week.
The mayor's office has issued the berserker a production order violation, which the berserker ate. The office considers the matter closed.
Overseer statement: 'An unhappy dwarf is a dwarf not yet given enough work.' Twelve new work orders have been queued for {first}, to help.
The sheriff, hammerer and dungeon master offices are all vacant, so justice is being administered by whatever is nearest, which is mostly a door.
Experts say berserk episodes follow long stretches of bad thoughts. Those on file include rain, gathering plants in the rain, and rain.
{who} was last seen chasing a hauler round the cistern. The hauler was carrying refuse to the garbage pit, the first time the pit has saved anyone.
The bookkeeper has added a 'damages' column to the ledger, between 'armor stands' and 'more armor stands'.
Elders recall a weaver who once went possessed waiting for a loom room. 'At least this one is getting exercise,' said one, from under a table.
Calm has returned to {fort}, chiefly because everyone is hiding. A mist ring session has been booked for the berserker, and for the dwarves who hid.
The episode was preceded by a long speech about the Overseer, the work orders and 'who exactly needs a thousand armor stands'. Many listeners nodded.

kickers.text: {first} is in a quiet room. Please let it stay quiet.
Bad thoughts may be lodged with the mist ring, not with fists.
The Overseer has queued an apology. It is an armor stand.
Hide behind the armor stands; at last they are useful.
Militia response time: pending the captain's nap.
The thrones will be righted when someone is assigned to right them.
A full report will follow once the reporter stops hiding.
Please, everyone, take a drink. A calm one.

heads.text: MOODY DWARF WANTS ROUGH GEMS. ANY?
EVERY GEM CUT; MOOD ARRIVES ON CUE
CHILD IN MOOD DEMANDS PLANT CLOTH
JEWELER BLAMED FOR CUTTING IT ALL
FEY DWARF CLAIMS LOOM ROOM AT LAST
MOOD DEMANDS THE ONE THING WE LACK

caps.text: The moody dwarf's request, in full: 'ROUGH.' Underlined four times.
The gem stockpile: every stone cut, polished and entirely useless to this dwarf.
A child in a strange mood, demanding plant cloth. The child is four.
The jeweler beside her work, trying very hard to look like she didn't do it.
The workshop door, barred. Behind it, a dwarf. Behind the dwarf, a need for something rough.
Haulers searching the old stockpiles for one rough gem. They found eight hundred loose stones.
The fey fisherdwarf, sketching a fish made of gems we no longer have.
The moody butcher, eyeing a sapphire that nobody can uncut.
A dwarf in a mood beside a thousand armor stands, wanting none of them.
The moody weaver at a free loom. Veterans of older forts in the doorway, applauding quietly.
Artist's map of where rough gems might remain. It is mostly the caverns. And a goblin.
The moody dwarf at sunrise, hour nineteen of staring. Still wants rough gems.

reps.text: {who} has been seized by a strange mood and asked, through the workshop door, for rough gems. Every gem in {fort} was cut last season, by standing order.
This is the fourth mood in a row to want the one material the fort just used up. Scholars call it coincidence. Moody dwarves call it 'typical'.
Readers recall a fey carpenter at Quakefocus who died of thirst beside 150 rough gems. This mood, by contrast, has the thirst but not the gems.
A dwarven child has fallen into a strange mood and demanded plant cloth. Parents say it is the most focused the child has ever been, meals included.
{first} has claimed a workshop and wants 'something rough, something precious, something the Overseer has not cut.' The jeweler has gone into hiding.
Miners went into the caverns for one rough gem and returned with stone. Stone, they argue, is rough. {first} disagrees, through the door.
The Overseer has answered the mood by queuing another round of gem cutting. The management insists this is unrelated and asks for no further questions.
Haulers searched the refuse pile, the old stockpiles and the garbage pit for anything uncut. They found a sock. The sock has been rejected.
The Herald recalls a possessed weaver at {past_fort} who died waiting for the loom room. This time the loom room is free, which officials call progress.
On the workshop wall the moody dwarf has drawn a gem, a log and something that may be a bone, a fish or the mayor. Haulers are bringing all three.
{liaison}, our liaison, writes that there is much to share and that rough gems may join next year's import agreement, at a modest double the price.
The workshop has been silent five days. Friends left a drink at the door. It is untouched, which this fort has learned to find alarming.
Scholars warn a moody dwarf left without materials may go insane. Scholars also note that this is {fort}, and that the odds are well known.
{who} has asked for rough gems, then cloth, then rough gems again. The cloth stockpile shows seven silk scraps, which veterans of {past_fort} say hide a shortage.

kickers.text: If you have a rough gem, slide it under the door.
The jeweler is excused from comment.
Next season the fort will run out of whatever the next mood wants.
{first} asks for privacy and one (1) uncut gem.
Please hold all gem cutting until further notice.
Children in moods are to be addressed as 'master'.
Leave a drink. Then make sure it gets drunk.
Rough gems available by import agreement, at a slight markup.

heads.text: NEW ARTIFACT; NOT AN ARMOR STAND
48 FIGURES LINE UP TO CLAIM IT
ARTIFACT HAS NAME; MAKER HAS NAP

caps.text: The new artifact on display, guarded by a cat and an armor stand, in order of usefulness.
The artifact beside Claspedserpent, the silver mace of Quakefocus. Each eyes the other.
The maker leaving the workshop after a week, asking only for a drink. Please give it.
Claimants queueing for the artifact. Famous artifacts draw dozens; we hope for fewer.
The artifact, drawn from memory, as the stockpile keeper will let nobody near it.
The artifact in its display case, which the Overseer ordered in a quantity of 400.
Spies of {enemy}, reading about the artifact in this very newspaper.
The workshop after the mood. Every scrap that was not a rough gem got used.
The engraving, showing the founding of {past_fort} and its slightly sad ending.
The maker's family posing with the artifact, which is clearly the favourite child.
The mayor, measuring the artifact for a production order violation.
The artifact being admired by an elf, who has been asked to stop touching it.

reps.text: {who} has emerged from a strange mood with a legendary artifact. Despite the Overseer's best efforts, it is not an armor stand, and it is not a throne.
Scholars rank the piece beside Claspedserpent, the silver mace of Quakefocus, and The Nuanced Hamlet, still at Searabbeys and still held by goblins.
The tavern already calls the artifact 'priceless', 'perfect' and 'the reason we are getting besieged next spring'.
Historians note The Amusing Duties, steel greaves lost at Roughnessslaps in year 68, has been claimed by some forty-eight figures. Ours has been claimed by one, so far.
{first} asks that the piece be displayed somewhere nobody can fall into, die of thirst beside or haul out of the garbage pit. A pedestal has been commissioned.
The Overseer has acknowledged the artifact by queuing 300 more display pedestals, should more artifacts need displaying. None are expected.
The mayor's office has fined the artifact for a production order violation, as it was never on the work orders. The artifact declined to pay.
Merchants offered a wagon of goods for the artifact. The bookkeeper politely declined, then asked whether the wagon was available separately.
Elders recall that the last fort's treasure stayed behind when the fort fell. 'Artifacts outlive forts,' they say. 'Try not to make that the theme again.'
The maker reports the work was 'exhausting, inspired and mostly done without a drink.' A drink has since been provided, and supervised.
The piece depicts, among other things, a dwarf drinking from a full barrel, which several readers have called 'aspirational'.
The outpost liaison writes that there is much to share and asks whether the artifact might be part of an import agreement. It might not.
Goblin scouts were seen loitering near {fort}, holding the Herald open at this page. The editor regrets nothing, and also everything.
The fort now owns more legendary items than militia members, a milestone officials describe as 'honestly not that hard'.

kickers.text: Goblins reading this: it is very heavy and very far away.
Please do not die of thirst admiring it.
Claims may be filed with the mayor, who will fine you.
The maker has been given a drink, under supervision.
It is not for trade, at any percentage.
Viewing hours: whenever the stockpile keeper is asleep.
{past_fort} lost its treasure. We intend to keep ours.
{first} accepts praise, drinks and rough gems.

heads.text: GENIUS AT WORK, IGNORED BY ORDERS
SKILL RISES; WORK ORDERS RISE MORE
GRAND WORK; NO DOCTOR TO ADMIRE

caps.text: The masterwork among a sea of ordinary armor stands, like a duck in a pond of ducks.
The craftsdwarf with the masterpiece. The masterpiece is the one looking smug.
A wall smoothed so perfectly that three dwarves have walked into it.
The finest throne in the fort, among a hundred others. You can tell by the glow.
The master's workshop, with the next forty work orders pinned to the door.
The masterwork mug. The first drink from it was ceremonial. The second, essential.
The mayor admiring the masterpiece while reaching for a citation pad, out of habit.
Fellow crafters applauding, while quietly revising their opinions of themselves.
The master's tools, laid out like surgical instruments, in a fort with no surgeon.
An elf calling the masterpiece 'acceptable'. The highest elven praise on record.
The master taking a well-earned break beside a well, drinking, as encouraged.
A close-up of the masterwork's detail. The artist's own detail is less good.

reps.text: {who} has produced a masterpiece. Of the eleven hundred armor stands made this season, critics say this one alone stands as if it means it.
The Overseer praised the masterwork and at once ordered four hundred more exactly like it, then queued them behind sixteen thousand smoothing jobs.
Veterans of {record_fort}, remembered for {record}, call the piece 'the first one I'd actually sit on, or hang a helm on.'
{first} says the secret to masterwork quality is 'practice, patience and a drink every few hours,' which the Herald prints here in large type for all.
The mayor's office praised the masterpiece and charged its maker with a production order violation for making only one. Both notices went out the same morning.
The piece was finished with the fort's very last rough gem, moments before a dwarf went into a strange mood and asked for the very last rough gem.
Haulers moved the masterwork to the stockpile with great care, then set a barrel on it. The barrel was full. Nobody drank from it.
Colleagues say {first} has been at the bench since the last migrant wave, pausing only to sleep and, at the Herald's urging, to drink.
Merchants want to buy it. {liaison}, our liaison, writes that there is much to share and suggests an import agreement for masterpieces, at double the price.
Elders compare it to the work of the old smiths of {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. 'Lock this one up,' they advise.
Tavern critics rate the masterpiece 'better than the thrones, worse than ale.' The maker accepts this as the highest grade available in {fort}.
A legendary smoother has finished a wall so perfect that the Overseer has asked for it to be smoothed again, to check.
The masterpiece now sits in the dining hall, improving every meal for those who can see it, which is mostly the cat.
With this masterwork, {fort} has one more legendary artisan than militia soldiers, a ratio the captain calls 'fine, honestly'.

kickers.text: The Overseer wants 400 more. Please do not tell the maker.
{first} accepts compliments and drinks, in that order.
Walk carefully; the walls are now dangerously smooth.
Masterworks cannot be traded for courage. We asked.
The maker requests no further work orders. Denied.
One good armor stand. Only a thousand to go.
Please drink from the masterwork mug. That is what it is for.
The Herald rates this item 'well made'. We rarely do.

heads.text: STRIKE THE EARTH, THEN SMOOTH IT
MINE HITS WATER; DWARVES STILL DRY
MINERS HIT IT BIG, KEEP DIGGING

caps.text: The miner's find. The jeweler was drawn outside the frame, for everyone's safety.
A pocket of rough gems, sketched quickly before anyone could cut them.
The vein, glittering. The Overseer's planned armor stands, glittering faintly in the future.
The miner pointing at ore and also, by accident, at a forgotten beast's front door.
The new tunnel, already queued for smoothing. All of it. Every surface.
Silver, the stuff of legendary maces. The veterans stood very still to look at it.
Miners celebrating underground, safely away from all trees.
The bookkeeper logging the find, just under {record} from {record_fort}.
The mine entrance, marked 'NOT SAFETY' to avoid confusion with the other deep hole.
The moodiest dwarf in the fort, peering in, asking if any of it is rough.
The miner's pick, retired to the tavern wall. It will be back at work by lunch.
The find, as imagined by goblins reading this paper. They have drawn it bigger.

reps.text: Miners have struck a pocket of rough gems. The jeweler was escorted from the area at once, and every dwarf with a history of moods has been told, quietly, to wait.
{who} hit the vein mid-swing and shouted 'Strike the earth!' The Overseer heard it and queued eleven hundred more digging jobs, to be thorough.
Elders call it the best find since {past_fort}, which had loose stones everywhere and still had a miner die of thirst. 'Hydrate,' they add.
The new tunnel is deep, though officials stress it is not thirty levels deep, and that nobody is to name any room down there 'Safety'.
The bookkeeper values the find at roughly a thousand armor stands, a unit of value the fort has, sadly, adopted.
Engineers warn deeper digging means caverns, and caverns mean forgotten beasts. Miners reply that it also means rough gems. The debate continues.
{liaison}, our liaison, writes that there is much to share and asks whether the ore might be exported at double the price. The miners replied with a gesture.
{first} reports striking the vein 'with one swing, and three days of swinging before it.' A drink was sent down, and {first} was watched until it was finished.
The mayor's office praised the strike and filed a production order violation, as the ore was found before the order to find it was issued.
{enemy} is believed to read the Herald. The Herald therefore reports the strike was small, dull and mostly gravel.
Silver has been found, the metal of Claspedserpent, the great mace of Quakefocus. The weaponsmiths are thrilled. The militia, all one of it, is asleep.
The ore stockpile is now full, and the overflow has been stacked in the throne room, among thrones one through a hundred.
The strike is so promising that the Overseer has ordered the tunnels smoothed, the smoothing engraved and the engravings, possibly, smoothed.
Miners are reminded the find is underground, which is the correct direction. Trees are the wrong direction. A miner on a branch has never struck anything.

kickers.text: Jewelers are asked to keep their hands in their pockets.
Rough gems are reserved for the next strange mood.
Goblins: it was gravel. Honestly.
Do not name the new tunnel 'Safety'.
Smoothing begins tomorrow and ends never.
{first} has earned a drink. Please make sure it is drunk.
Next stop: the caverns, and whatever lives there.
Value of find: roughly {record}.

heads.text: "IS IT ALWAYS LIKE THIS?" ASK NEW

caps.text: The migrant wave, arriving at a fort with a thousand armor stands and no armor.
Newcomers at the gate, handed their work orders before their names.
A migrant asking the way to the Safety burrow. A local shaking his head slowly.
New arrivals touring the throne room: a hundred thrones, each claimed by nobody.
Refugees who have seen {enemy} up close and would rather not again.
The migrants' wagon, empty of rough gems, to the visible dismay of a moody dwarf.
Newcomers on their first job: smoothing. Their second job will also be smoothing.
The welcome committee: the mayor, with a pad of production order violation forms.
A migrant child, already eyeing the workshops. Parents have been warned.
New arrivals at the well, which old residents walk past daily. Learn, newcomers.
Migrants meeting the militia captain, who woke up long enough to wave.
New dormitory beds, ordered in a quantity the Overseer called 'sensible': 900.

reps.text: A wave of migrants has arrived at {fort}, bringing the population to {pop}. Each has been issued a bed, a mug and a list of 140 smoothing jobs.
Several newcomers are refugees from towns taken by The Crazed Hex. They asked whether the fort had walls, then whether it had a militia, then went quiet.
Migrants were met at the gate by a letter from the liaison saying there is much to share. Nobody knows what was shared. The newcomers kept their bags close.
{who} arrived with the wave and asked where the drinks are kept. Veterans explained they are kept everywhere, and that this has never helped anyone.
The newcomers toured the highlights: the windmills, the mist ring, the cistern, the catacombs, the execution tower and the thousand armor stands.
A migrant volunteered for the vacant office of sheriff. Officials were so startled the paperwork was lost, and the office is vacant again.
Newcomers keen on the militia were told nine places are open, all permanently Off duty. Three signed up. Nobody has told the captain.
One family has followed the fort since {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}. 'We follow the fort,' they said. 'And the drinks.'
The Overseer welcomed the migrants by queuing three hundred beds and three thousand armor stands, which the management describes as 'balanced'.
Newcomers have been taught local custom: do not climb trees, do not shelter thirty levels down, do not haul refuse out of the pit, and do drink.
Some migrants hail from human towns and asked why the smoothers smooth walls nobody sees. They were told: 'The Overseer.' They have stopped asking.
The bookkeeper has entered the newcomers in a column labelled 'hope'. The previous column, labelled 'more hope', is already full.
A migrant child has been seen staring at the workshops with a strange expression. Parents are advised to hide any plant cloth they may have.
The new wave arrived in {season}, carrying their worldly goods and, regrettably, not one single rough gem.

kickers.text: Welcome. Your first smoothing job begins immediately.
Newcomers: the well is the round thing. Please use it.
Militia sign-ups now open. Nobody has told the captain.
Please do not unpack in the Safety burrow.
Population up; armor stands per dwarf, sadly, down.
{first} has already been cited by the mayor. Welcome home.
Refugees: you are among friends, and thrones.
Trees are decorative. Do not climb the decorations.

heads.text: DEPOT FULL OF STANDS, NOT GOODS
TRADERS SELL ROUGH GEMS AT LAST?

caps.text: The liaison, mid-sentence. The sentence is 'There is much to share.' It always is.
Merchants inspecting the 300 armor stands we offered. They took one, as a favour.
The depot, buried under thrones. The traders had to climb.
A merchant wagon fresh from the road past the burned towns, still visibly nervous.
The broker, haggling. Behind him, a thousand reasons the fort needs to sell something.
Elves from the forest retreat, examining our wooden goods with open disapproval.
A wagon of meat, greeted by veterans of the long meatless years with real tears.
The trader's scale. On one side, rings. On the other, a 210% markup.
Humans from Toeembrace, of The Fair Cakes, who did not bring cakes. We checked.
Pack animals at the depot, given the mist ring treatment and, frankly, loving it.
The broker's ledger, mostly crossed out, with 'MORE?' written at the bottom.
Haulers carrying goods to the depot by the longest route available: via a tree.

reps.text: The outpost liaison opened by saying there is much to share. The fort's few officials nodded, braced, and waited for the import agreement.
Traders asked to buy rings at 210% of value. The broker said the fort has no rings. The traders said that was exactly why they were offering 210%.
The broker offered the merchants three hundred armor stands. After some discussion they accepted one, on condition they would not have to carry it.
Merchants say the road was hazardous: {enemy} has been busy. They charged a '{enemy_race} fee', which the bookkeeper still disputes.
{who} was assigned to haul goods to the depot and was later found across the map gathering plants in the rain. The goods remain unhauled.
The caravan brought meat. Elders who lived through the long meatless years wept openly and asked whether it came in sausage form.
Elven traders praised the fort for sparing the trees, then grew concerned on learning the decision was the Overseer's and entirely accidental.
Traders were offered a throne and asked how many we had. On hearing the number, they offered to take three at a discount, for the novelty.
The liaison recommends an import agreement for spears, rough gems and 'one competent sheriff'. The mayor calls it the most useful document of the year.
A merchant quietly asked whether The Grooved Council still holds Jackaldefense. It does. Prices went up.
Haulers carried goods so slowly that the caravan nearly left. The Overseer blamed the haulers. The haulers blamed the ten thousand smoothing jobs ahead of them.
The broker traded a stone mug for a barrel of ale, bringing the fort to two thousand and one drinks and making the bookkeeper laugh for the first time this year.
Merchants report {civ} is at peace with most of the world, and that all of it has heard about the armor stands.
The caravan left {fort} in {season}, heavier by one throne and lighter by every barrel of anything resembling meat.

kickers.text: There is, as ever, much to share.
Armor stands remain available, in volume.
Next caravan: please bring rough gems and a doctor.
The import agreement is under review, by nobody.
Ring prices remain at double. We have no rings.
Haulers are reminded the depot is not in a tree.
{first} has been commended for haggling, and eventually for hauling.
Meat watch suspended pending sausages.

heads.text: BABY BORN; ALREADY WANTS A MOOD
BIRTH GOES FINE; NO DOCTOR NEEDED
BABY NOW EQUALS MILITIA IN SIZE

caps.text: The newborn, asleep in a cradle the Overseer ordered in a batch of 600.
The proud parents with the baby and, behind them, a hundred thrones nobody has sat on.
The baby's first look at the fort. Its expression is the one the Herald wears daily.
The infant drinking milk, on time, without being told. A model citizen already.
The nursery, smoothed to perfection by smoothers with ten thousand other jobs.
The baby meeting the militia captain. Both were asleep.
The infant gripping a rough gem. Moody dwarves in the background, watching.
The midwife: no doctor, but a very confident hauler with clean hands.
The baby's first toy: a tiny armor stand. Of course it was.
The nursery door, marked 'NOT SAFETY' to settle everyone's nerves.
The family tree, drawn as a family stone, as trees are not trusted here.
The mayor presenting the baby with its first production order violation.

reps.text: {who} has welcomed a baby. The infant was born healthy, hungry and thirsty, and has already learned to drink when thirsty, unlike some adults in {fort}.
The birth went ahead without a doctor, as the chief medical dwarf's office is vacant. A hauler supervised, then asked for the office, and was refused.
The population now stands at {pop}: one more dwarf than yesterday, and one fewer armor stand per dwarf than the Overseer would like.
The Overseer marked the birth by queuing 600 cradles and a toy armor stand for every child the fort may ever have. The order is already running away.
Parents say the baby cries at the windmills, coos at the mist ring and stares, unblinking, at the gem stockpile. Moody dwarves are watching closely.
The fort's children have a record of strange moods; one demanded plant cloth. Parents are advised to stock some now, just in case.
The mayor congratulated the family and cited the infant for a production order violation, having produced only noise. The fine is one rattle.
The baby received the traditional gifts: a mug, a blanket and a stern warning about trees.
Grandparents who remember {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}, call the child 'our first born in a fort we haven't had to leave yet'.
{first} describes the baby as 'perfect, loud and already tired of the Overseer.' The Herald notes this is a typical first impression.
The militia captain visited the newborn and offered it a place in the squad. Given the nine vacancies, the offer is considered sincere.
The baby was born in {season}. It will be shown the surface by spring and told never to gather plants out there in the rain.
The nursery sits far from the garbage pit, the deep stairs and every tree. It is, by some distance, the safest room in {fort}.
The bookkeeper has entered the baby under 'future haulers'. The baby has entered itself in the ledger under 'spilled ink'.

kickers.text: The baby asks for no visitors and a drink. Smart baby.
Keep plant cloth on hand. Just in case.
Congratulations, and welcome to the work queue.
The baby is not to be stored in an armor stand.
{first} is resting. The baby is not.
Gifts of rough gems will be held for the inevitable mood.
No trees for the baby. Ever.
Born in {fort}, and staying, the gods willing.

heads.text: TWO DWARVES, ONE BEDROOM, NO FORM
MILITIA OF ONE SERVES AS USHER

caps.text: The happy couple, standing before a hundred thrones and sitting on none.
The wedding feast: every dish the kitchen had, and two thousand drinks nobody touched.
The vows, as recited. The second line is 'and to drink regularly'.
The couple's new bedroom, freshly smoothed by a smoother who was not invited.
Wedding gifts: a mug, a blanket and, from the Overseer, forty armor stands.
The militia captain, serving as usher and also, briefly, as a sleeping guest.
The mayor with a citation pad, attending in an official capacity, uninvited.
Guests dancing beside the mist ring. Damp, but delighted.
The couple's first look as spouses. Behind them, the job board, glaring.
The ring, borrowed, as the fort had none and the depot wanted double for one.
The wedding cake, which is a roast, because this is a fortress.
The best dwarf's speech, mostly about the time the groom got stuck in a tree.

reps.text: {who} has married in a ceremony attended by friends, family and a long list of work orders the Overseer declined to postpone.
The couple wed in the dining hall in {season}, promising to love, to honour, and never to shelter in a burrow named Safety.
The Overseer marked the union with six hundred matching mugs and four hundred armor stands. The couple's bedroom can now hold neither the couple nor the gift.
The mayor's office congratulated the pair and cited them for a production order violation, as weddings appear nowhere on the work orders.
Guests report a brief ceremony, a long feast and enthusiastic drinking, which elders call the healthiest thing to happen in {fort} all year.
{first} says the couple met hauling the same stone in opposite directions for a season. 'We kept bumping into each other. Then we kept doing it on purpose.'
No priest was available, so the bookkeeper conducted the ceremony, reading the vows from the ledger and then counting the guests, twice.
The militia captain served as usher and remained Off duty throughout, which guests agree is the most active the captain has been in seasons.
The couple will honeymoon in their bedroom, which the Overseer has thoughtfully queued for re-smoothing during the honeymoon.
Elders of {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}, wept at the ceremony. 'We had weddings there too,' one said. 'Then we had goblins.'
The pair asked for no gifts, only that every guest drink something today, slowly, in front of witnesses.
Rings were sought at the depot, where traders quoted double the price. The couple instead exchanged two very nice rocks.
Both families are said to be thrilled. The cats are said to be indifferent, which is how cats attend weddings.
{civ} sent congratulations by letter, along with a reminder about this year's export quotas, which the couple has framed.

kickers.text: The couple requests privacy and fewer work orders.
Gifts of drink are welcome, if actually drunk.
{first} has asked us not to mention the tree story. Sorry.
Gift armor stands may be returned for credit. There is no shop.
The honeymoon is scheduled between smoothing jobs.
Love: the one order the Overseer did not queue.
Congratulations, and do not move into a burrow called Safety.
The mayor's citation is the couple's first joint possession.

heads.text: GHOST DEMANDS SLAB, AND A DRINK
GHOST OF THE TREE MINER RETURNS

caps.text: The ghost drifting through the drinks stockpile, which it can now see clearly. Too late.
A thirsty spirit pointing at a barrel. Witnesses say the barrel looked guilty.
The ghost seated in the tree it died in, refusing to come down even now.
The Safety burrow, now haunted, and somehow even less safe.
The phantom hauler, still carrying refuse up out of the garbage pit.
The spirit inspecting the slab queue. Its slab is at position four hundred.
A ghost walking past a thousand armor stands, to which it has no objection.
The spectral miner, clutching a pick and a mug, both empty.
The ghost visiting the hospital, which also lacks a doctor in the afterlife.
The ghost and the militia captain, both on duty for once. Well, one of them.
The spirit of a Searabbeys miner, still dehydrated, still looking for the drinks.
The mason, finally engraving the slab, with a ghost reading over his shoulder.

reps.text: The ghost of {first} has been drifting through the cellars, pointing at full barrels and moaning. Scholars believe it is not angry, merely making a point.
A restless spirit has moved into the Safety burrow, far below the fort. Officials say this does not change the burrow's safety rating, which was already 'none'.
{who} has returned as a ghost and resumed hauling refuse out of the garbage pit. Haulers are still throwing more in. Nothing has been learned on either side.
A ghost sits in a tree near the gate, refusing to come down. The miner it once was also refused to come down, which is, sadly, the whole story.
The mason has been told to engrave a slab at once. The Overseer has queued it after four hundred armor stands, which the ghost is reported to have heard.
Visitors say a ghost from {past_fort}, which {past_fort_fate}, has wandered in looking for its old bedroom. It was given a spare and seems content to sulk there.
The ghost of {first} has been seen smoothing walls at night. Smoothers call the work excellent and have asked whether it would like to stay on.
Priests advise a slab. The bookkeeper advises a slab. The ghost, through a series of thrown mugs, also advises a slab.
The spirit stands by the well, staring at it, then at the living, then at the well again. Several dwarves took the hint and had a drink.
The mayor's office cited the ghost for loitering. The ghost passed through the citation, and the mayor, without signing.
A ghost has joined the militia, filling one of the nine vacant places. It is the first squad member in years to attend every drill.
Reports from the dining hall describe cold spots, toppled chairs and a voice saying 'it was RIGHT THERE.' The barrel in question has been moved.
The ghost is thought to be a dwarf who died in a hospital with no doctor. It now haunts the vacant chief medical dwarf's office, pointedly.
Elders say ghosts in {fort} are restless because 'they all died of something silly'. The Herald calls this unkind, and also broadly accurate.

kickers.text: The slab is queued behind the armor stands. Sorry.
Drink now, so you need not haunt the cellar later.
{first} remains thirsty, which is no longer anyone's fault.
The ghost asks that we stop throwing refuse into the pit.
Haunted trees will be chopped down, eventually.
Engrave a slab, and spare us all the moaning.
Ghost drill attendance: perfect. Living attendance: one, asleep.
The living are reminded: it was right there.

heads.text: MINER ESCAPES TO A TREE. UH-OH.
GARBAGE PIT GROWS A NEW LEVEL

caps.text: The collapse, seen from below. The artist has asked not to be assigned below again.
The ceiling, mid-fall. It had been smoothed beautifully. It was a shame.
A thousand armor stands, unscratched beneath the rubble. They are, it turns out, sturdy.
The dig plan, showing one channel order repeated four hundred times.
The rescue team, digging. Behind them, the job board, adding more digging.
The tunnel, now a ramp, now a pit, now a matter for the bookkeeper.
A miner in a tree after fleeing the collapse. We know how this ends. Please come down.
The garbage pit, one level deeper. Haulers have been told, though not why.
Dust clearing over the throne room. Some of the thrones are now lower thrones.
The drinks stockpile, untouched by the collapse and, as usual, by everyone else.
The engineer's diagram of what went wrong: a single arrow pointing at the Overseer.
The new cavern opening, from which something is almost certainly watching.

reps.text: A tunnel collapsed after the Overseer queued four hundred channeling jobs on one square. Engineers say the square is now fully channeled, and then some.
The collapse buried a whole workshop of armor stands. Rescuers report the armor stands are unharmed, unlike morale.
{who} was smoothing a wall when the ceiling above came down. The wall, witnesses say, was left very smooth, and the smoother is recovering nicely.
Rubble now blocks the stairs to the Safety burrow. Residents are split on whether this is a disaster or the best safety measure the burrow has ever had.
Engineers believe the cave-in followed the removal of a support pillar, which the work order described as 'unnecessary stone'.
The Overseer has answered the collapse by queuing the rubble for smoothing, the smoothing for engraving, and the engravers for a long talk.
The collapse opened a hole into the caverns, now sealed with a door taken from a hospital, which had no doctor but did have a door.
Miners caught in the collapse report that at no point were they short of rock. 'Drink, sometimes,' one said. 'Rock, never.'
A miner fled the cave-in by climbing a tree on the surface. Rescuers are working to get the miner down before the fort's traditional tree-related ending.
The mayor's office has cited the ceiling for a production order violation, as it fell without being ordered to. The ceiling has not responded.
Elders say a collapse is how {past_fort} first learned it had caverns. They add that {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}, and that the two facts may be related.
The bookkeeper reports the cave-in added three hundred loose stones to stock, bringing the total to 'more than anyone needs, ever'.
The garbage pit has partly collapsed into the level below, which was the bedroom level. Residents are asked to check their beds before sleeping.
Every trapped dwarf has been dug out and returned to {fort}, where each was promptly reassigned to the digging job that caused the collapse.

kickers.text: Please do not dig out the pillar. It is holding things.
Rubble has been queued for smoothing, naturally.
The armor stands are fine. Thank you for asking.
Climbing a tree is not an evacuation plan.
Those under the rubble: shout, and we will come eventually.
Safety burrow access: improved, by being blocked.
The ceiling has been cited. The ceiling does not care.
New loose stones available, in bulk, forever.

caps.text: The soldier, mid-drill, alone in a barracks built for ten.
The squad roster: one name and nine very neat blank lines.
The training dummy, retiring with dignity and a great many dents.
The soldier's armor, taken off an armor stand. One of a thousand. Finally, a use.
The soldier on guard at the gate. The schedule says Off duty. The soldier disagrees.
The champion's office, vacant, with a soldier eyeing the chair.
The mayor congratulating the soldier with a citation for 'unscheduled training'.
The soldier drinking water between drills, the only dwarf with a regular habit.
Empty weapon racks, being filled by the soldier, one axe at a time.
The soldier posing with the fort's artifact. Neither has ever fought a goblin.
The soldier sparring with a ghost, the only other squad member available for drills.
A goblin, far away, hearing about this and adjusting its plans, very slightly.

reps.text: {who} has achieved legendary skill at arms, making {first} the finest soldier in a militia of exactly one. The nine empty places have been informed by memo.
The captain was found awake and training this week, which the barracks have formally recorded as an event. The schedule has been checked for errors.
The training dummy has conceded after a full season of drills and asked to be moved to the armor stand stockpile, where life is quieter.
The champion's office remains vacant. {first} is welcome to apply, once the office's paperwork is found beneath the mayor's citations.
The Overseer has marked the soldier's rise by queuing nine more weapon racks, two hundred spears and no new soldiers.
{first} says the secret is 'drills, sleep and a drink every few hours,' which the Herald prints again here, in case anyone missed it in the obituaries.
With a master of arms in the barracks, {fort} is now safe from any enemy that arrives one at a time, near the barracks, during duty hours.
The soldier has requested a squad. The mayor's office wants the request in triplicate. The soldier asked whether the mayor would like to spar.
Elders recall that {past_fort} also had one good soldier, and that {past_fort} {past_fort_fate}. 'One is not enough,' they say. 'Ask the other nine.'
News of the achievement is thought to have reached {enemy}. The Herald hopes it arrived as 'a large army' rather than 'one dwarf, usually asleep'.
The soldier's armor came from the armor stand stockpile, the first armor stand in living memory to hold armor and then give it up for a good cause.
{who} has trained since {season}, sparring with the dummy, the wall and, on one memorable night, a ghost who happened to be passing.
{civ} has been told of the new legend and replied with congratulations and a request that the soldier escort the next caravan, alone.
Militia command, which is to say {first}, has declared the fort's defences 'improved by roughly one dwarf', which is all of them.

kickers.text: The other nine places remain open. Please apply.
{first} is training. Please do not mention the schedule.
The dummy has asked for a quieter life. Granted.
Enemies are asked to arrive one at a time.
The champion's office is vacant. {first}, take the hint.
One armor stand has finally done its job.
Militia strength: up from one tired dwarf to one excellent one.
Next season: perhaps a second soldier. Dream big.
